claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a coarse, as-solidified microstructure.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is prone to cracking.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response under magnetic-field and pressure-field operation.
Cold rolling followed by tailored annealing will refine the alloy's grain structure.
The proposed treatment can retain the phase chemistry and transformation characteristics responsible for the caloric effects.
The treatment will produce smaller, more uniformly distributed grains.
The treatment will produce coherent or semi-coherent grain boundaries.
Refined grains and the resulting grain-boundary network will blunt crack propagation.
Reducing average grain size and increasing grain-boundary area will impede crack initiation and propagation.
Impeded crack initiation and propagation will increase toughness and cracking resistance.
Within an optimized grain-size window, transition temperatures and transformation entropy changes will remain largely unaffected.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have higher fracture toughness than the as-cast alloy.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have a lower fatigue crack-growth rate under cyclic loading than the as-cast alloy.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will preserve a caloric-response magnitude similar to that of the as-cast alloy under identical magnetic-field and pressure-field conditions.
The intervention is expected to be effective under cyclic mechanical loading.
The intervention is intended to apply near room temperature or within the alloy's active caloric regime.
The intervention is intended to apply over the magnetic-field and pressure ranges used in the alloy's refrigeration cycle.
